purpose: Quantify how many MFR2 identities also appear in the ROF training split, so the manuscript's cross-dataset claim is evidence-based.
method: Exact normalised name match. 'aggressive' strips all non-alphanumeric characters (joe_biden -> joebiden); 'light' only collapses spaces, underscores and hyphens and trims.

light_normalisation.note: The single match depends on the normalisation chosen; under strict name matching the two sets are disjoint.

context_all_rof_splits.note: Across train+val+test (182 persons) the intersection is 2.

conclusion: MFR2 is not fully identity-disjoint from ROF training, but the overlap is small: one identity, 18 of 820 pairs (2.2%). The manuscript previously described this as 'substantial overlap', which the evidence does not support.
